newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were steady with some regional short-dates buying and others sidelined ahead of the release of the U.S. jobless claims and retail sales data on Thursday, dealers said on Tuesday.

The U.S. jobless claims for August shows a forecast of 5.1 percent as compared to July's 5.4 percent and the retail sales figure is expected to show an increase of 0.2 percent compared with a 0.1 percent rise in July.
"The market was fairly quiet today. I think this was due mainly to the soft rates which do not attract investors," a local dealer said.
"Some traders are also waiting for the release of the U.S. jobless claims and retail sales data for (clues to) market direction," he added.
In day-to-day rates, Tuesday/Wednesday remained unchanged at 5-1/4 5-1/8 percent. Week-fixed eased 3/16 percentage point to 5-3/8 5-1/4 from 5-1/4 5-1/8 percent.

Among longer dates, one-month and three-months remained unchanged at 5-3/8 5-1/4, 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, respectively. Six-months was also unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent. Nine-months and twelve-months were also steady at 5-13/16 5-11/16, 5-9/16 5-11/16 percent, respectively. -- M.Ling
